query: What is the current status of SpaceX Starship Flight 13 (IFT-13) as of mid-July 2026? Has Booster 20 completed its static fire test? Has the FAA approved Flight 13 / accepted the Flight 12 mishap investigation? What is the latest NET (no earlier than) launch date shown on trackers like NextSpaceflight and RGV Aerial Photography?
answer:
I've completed the research on SpaceX Starship Flight 13. Here's the summary of findings as of mid-July 2026:

## Key Answers to Your Questions

**Has Booster 20 completed its static fire?** ✅ **YES** — Booster 20 completed a full-duration 33-engine static fire on **July 10, 2026** at Pad 2, Starbase (NASASpaceflight called it "record duration").

**Has the FAA approved Flight 13 / accepted the Flight 12 mishap investigation?** ✅ **YES** — The FAA **closed the Flight 12 mishap investigation and accepted SpaceX's findings on July 13, 2026**, clearing Flight 13 to proceed. The Flight 12 booster loss (May 22 flight) was blamed on heat effects on propulsion components and erroneous engine alarm settings; no public injury or property damage.

**Latest NET launch date?** **Monday, July 20, 2026, at 22:45 UTC (6:45 p.m. EDT)** from Pad 2, Starbase. This is confirmed consistently across NextSpaceflight (details/8279), Space.com, WAI Hub, and RocketLaunch.Live.

## Critical Development
A first launch attempt on **July 16, 2026 was aborted at T-0** when four Raptor 3 engines failed to meet starting parameters (automatic software abort). Elon Musk said two Raptors would be swapped out, pushing the NET from July 16 to **July 20**.

## Vehicles & Mission
- **Booster 20** (Super Heavy V3) + **Ship 40** (Starship V3) — second flight of Starship V3
- Payload: first deployment of **20 V3 Starlink satellites**
- Possibly the final suborbital Starship test flight before orbital attempts

**Note:** I couldn't directly access RGV Aerial Photography, but all major trackers converge on the July 20 NET. All data reflects reporting through ~July 17, 2026; the July 20 date remains subject to weather and the engine swap.

key_facts: Flight 13 uses Booster 20 (Super Heavy V3) and Ship 40 (Starship V3); it is the second flight of Starship V3.
Booster 20 completed a full-duration 33-engine static fire on July 10, 2026 at Pad 2, Starbase (described as record-duration; ~25 seconds per WAI Hub).
Ship 40 completed cryogenic proof tests (May 4-5) and a ~60-second static fire on July 1, 2026.
The FAA closed and accepted SpaceX's Flight 12 mishap investigation on July 13, 2026, clearing Flight 13 to proceed.
Flight 12 (flown May 22, 2026) booster loss was attributed to heat effects on propulsion components during ascent and erroneous engine alarm system settings; no public injury or property damage.
The first Flight 13 launch attempt on July 16, 2026 was aborted at T-0 when four Raptor 3 engines failed to meet starting parameters (automatic software abort).
Elon Musk said two Raptor engines would be removed and replaced before the next attempt.
Latest NET launch date is Monday, July 20, 2026 at 22:45 UTC (6:45 p.m. EDT) from Pad 2, Starbase, Texas.
Trackers NextSpaceflight, Space.com, WAI Hub, and RocketLaunch.Live all show NET July 20, 2026, 22:45 UTC.
Mission plans to deploy 20 V3 Starlink satellites and may be the final suborbital Starship test flight before orbital attempts.
